core_theme: 在 .NET 10 里给 HttpClient 加容错之前，先按正确顺序打好连接复用底子，再决定哪些请求可以被重试：一次下单被下游存成三条，是重试顺序错误的代价。
reader_takeaway: 读完之后能明白：先让请求走同一批复用的连接，再用标准容错处理器兜底，最后关掉不安全方法（POST）的默认重试并排好处理器顺序，重复下单才会收住。
summary_angle: 一次下单，下游却存了三条：先用连接复用打底（500 次请求后 socket 不再堆积），再用标准容错处理器兜底，最后靠关掉不安全方法的默认重试和排好处理器顺序，把重复下单切断。

final_prompt:
Use case: infographic-story
Asset type: wide cover infographic illustration for a Chinese tech blog article
Primary request: Create a wide cinematic infographic-story cover illustration that summarizes a .NET 10 HttpClient resilience-and-retry-order article. Theme: how HTTP client resilience is stacked in the right order — reuse connections first, then rely on the standard resilience handler, then stop the default retry on unsafe methods and order the handlers correctly. The reader should quickly feel the core irony: 一次下单，下游却存了三条。

Summary angle: 一条订单只提交一次，却在下游被存成三条重复记录。Left to right, in three beats: reuse connections so requests travel one shared pipeline (500 requests, no socket buildup), the standard resilience handler as the safety net, and finally switching off the default retry for unsafe methods to cut the duplicate writes.
Narrative flow: 3-beat process, left to right, one dominant focal subject plus three supporting beats in a 2.35:1 frame. Each beat must map to the article's information blocks rather than generic decoration.
Information blocks:
- problem (no visible label): 500 requests created with a fresh HttpClient leave 500 TIME_WAIT sockets piled up on the far left; show a row of pixel pipe mouths jamming shut under load
- mechanism (visible label: 0 残留): IHttpClientFactory reuses the same connections, so the same 500 requests leave 0 residual sockets; one continuous pixel conveyor pipe loops back on itself and stays clean
- contrast (visible label: 1 单 3 条): the default resilience pipeline stores 1 order as 3 identical rows downstream; a pixel warehouse shelf holds three identical wooden crates side by side, this shelf is the main focal subject
- takeaway (visible label: 关掉重试): DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods turns off the default retry for POST; a pixel valve/switch at the end of the conveyor is flipped to the closed position, cutting the resend loop

Main metaphor: a pixel-level stage pipeline — a jammed old pipe on the left, one reused conveyor in the middle, a shelf on the right where the same order is duplicated into three crates, and a switch at the end that cuts the retry loop.
Subject: a pixel-art order crate travelling along the reused conveyor, and the three identical copies it becomes on the right-hand shelf.
Composition/framing: diagonal left-to-right wide scene; the primary focal point is the shelf with the three duplicated crates; the other beats sit along the same horizontal line and stay legible in a very wide cover. Not a vertical poster, not a multi-panel collage.
Style/medium: combine editorial technical illustration with the selected visual style descriptor: retro pixel-art inspired illustration, blocky forms, limited palette, old game composition cues, readable wide layout. Stylized, polished, editorial, visually strong, and clearly readable as an infographic-style summary cover. Do not imitate a specific brand, studio, or living artist.
Color palette: deep ink green and dark charcoal base, amber-orange as the conveyor key light, teal-green highlight for the clean reused pipeline, brick red used only for the three duplicated crates.
Visible text policy: allow only the three short Chinese labels listed above ("0 残留", "1 单 3 条", "关掉重试"), each 6 characters or fewer, plus nothing else. No poster title, no headline, no long sentences, no English slogans or English labels, no fake UI labels, no fake chart axes, no fake architecture node names, no fabricated metrics.
Constraints: no watermark, no prompt residue, no screenshots, no dashboards, no fake diagrams, no fake charts, no fake terminal output, no fabricated metrics, no unrelated icon collage, no decorative clutter.
Avoid: poster title, English slogan, floating chips, code rain, neon skyline, generic robot poses, cyberpunk purple-blue glow, dense HUD overlays, fictional product screenshots.
